[[Mandarin Chinese|Mandarin]] | budget = | gross = }} '''''A New Old Play''''' ({{zh|t=椒麻堂會|link=no}}) is a 2021 [[epic film]] directed and written by [[Qiu Jiongjiong]]. As Qiu's seventh film, it marks his first [[narrative film|fictional feature]]. A co-production between Hong Kong's Uluka Productions and France's Hippocampe Productions, the film stars Yi Sicheng as Qiu Fu, a recently deceased [[Sichuan opera]] actor, alongside Guan Nan, Qiu Zhimin, Gu Tao, and Xue Xuchun. The story chronicles Qiu Fu's life and career in [[History of China#Modern China|China from the 1920s to the 1980s]] through his remembrances during his journey into the [[Youdu|netherworld]], featuring events such as the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], the [[Chinese Civil War]], the [[Great Chinese Famine]], and the [[Cultural Revolution]]. Qiu Jiongjiong conceived of the project in 2017 after illustrating the [[biography]] for his grandfather and Sichuan opera actor Qiu Fu. Inspired to tell the story with film, Qiu based the protagonist on his grandfather and began developing a screenplay from May 2017 to February 2018 under the [[working title]] ''The Neo-New Adventures''. Production design spanned six months before [[principal photography]] began in August 2019 in [[Leshan]], [[Sichuan]] over three months. Post-production took place in France, with French filmmaker {{ill|Marie-Pierre Duhamel-Muller|fr|Marie-Pierre Duhamel-Muller}} involved in the editing. The film also marks the second film to be primarily in [[Sichuanese dialects|Sichuanese]], after the 1962 film ''Conscription''. ''A New Old Play'' had its world premiere in competition for the [[Golden Leopard]] at the [[74th Locarno Film Festival]] on 13 August 2021, where it received the [[Special Jury Prize (Locarno International Film Festival)|Special Jury Prize]]. It also garnered various accolades and received positive reviews from critics, with praises particularly on its themes, narrative style and complexities, and production design. Due to [[Film censorship in China|censorship in China]], only single-time private screenings were held worldwide from 2021 to 2022. The film received its first [[wide release]] in France on 30 April 2025. == Plot == Qiu Fu, a renowned [[Sichuan opera]] actor, meets his demise. [[Ox-Head and Horse-Face]] are sent to escort him into the [[Youdu|netherworld]] to perform for [[Yanluo Wang]]. Qiu refuses to accept his fate and tries to flee, much to the envoys' confusion as they ask him how he, who has been an artiste since the age of eight, does not embrace death. Qiu retorts that he began his opera journey at seven and starts to reminisce about his life. During the [[Warlord Era]], an operaphile Pocky rises through the ranks to become a military commander. He uses his newfound power to form an opera troupe called the New-New Theatre School. Early in its operation, Qiu Fu, a foundling of a famous opera actor who died performing on stage, is sent to the troupe by his mother, who abandons him to remarry. Qiu learns opera singing from the troupe's teachers, but his performances are unsatisfactory. One day, while practising, he encounters Pocky, who takes a liking to him and accepts him as an apprentice. After some training, Qiu debuts as an opera performer. The [[Second World War]] soon breaks out, and the troupe begins charity tours to raise funds against [[Second Sino-Japanese War|Japan's invasion]]. One night, Qiu is intoxicated after drinking a bowl of poisonous mushroom soup and dreams of flying across the city on a leaf, only to be bombed by a Japanese fighter jet. In the netherworld, Qiu follows the envoys to the [[Pre-existence#Chinese mythology|Naihe Bridge]], where he encounters Crooky, a servant of the troupe who mysteriously disappeared decades ago. The envoys explain that they never received orders to take Crooky, but he keeps returning to the netherworld, trapping his soul between realms. He opens an inn at the Naihe Bridge to welcome both the deceased and [[Yaoguai|demons]]. Qiu decides to reunite with Crooky and stays at the inn while watching his young apprentices perform [[Chinese funeral rituals|rituals]] in the living world. Dissatisfied with their performances, he reminisces about his own early career. By 1945, Qiu has established himself as an opera actor. However, Pocky, now a [[warlord]], worries about his fate under [[Chiang Kai-shek]]'s rule and loses interest in opera. Before [[Chinese Civil War#Immediate post-war clashes (1945–1946)|the Civil War]], he disbands the troupe to protect the actors and their families from his impending downfall. Unemployed, Qiu's life worsens even after the establishment of the [[People's Republic of China]], when the troupe is reformed and renamed the People's Sichuan Opera Troupe. Qiu's daughter dies subsequently during the [[Great Chinese Famine]], but his son Hei survives. One day, Qiu finds [[Female infanticide in China|an abandoned infant girl]] on the street and, despite his meager living conditions, takes her in. He and his wife struggle to feed her and resort to stealing [[Human feces|feces]], only to be caught by [[Cadre system of the Chinese Communist Party|cadres]] who accuse them of stealing [[Public property|state property]]. Qiu sings to the cadres, leveraging his fame as an actor to escape. They manage to cook the [[maggots]] found in the feces to feed the girl, sustaining her life. Later, the girl's mother returns, claiming she abandoned her only because her husband tried to eat the child. Though reluctant, Qiu's wife returns the baby. During the [[Cultural Revolution]], the New-New troupe is [[Cultural Revolution#Opera and music|labeled as feudal]], [[Struggle session|facing persecution]] from the [[Red Guards]]. Hei, now a teenager, wishes to join the [[Great Exchange of Revolutionary Experience|Big Link-up]] in [[Beijing]] but is locked up by his family. Desperate, he escapes through a window and flies across the city on a leaf. Years later, now a high-ranking Red Guard, Hei returns home and learns that Qiu is released from [[Re-education through labor|labor]] and assigned to minor roles in plays. After reminiscing about his career, Qiu bids farewell to Crooky and shares one last drink with the envoys. Confused about how he will remember all his lines after drinking the [[Meng Po|Meng-po soup]], he is reassured by the envoys that his artistic intuition will guide him. Qiu boards the boat and reaches the other side, queuing for the Meng-po soup before drinking it all. The [[Movie camera|camera]] pans to each of the other characters drinking the soup at various moments, then returns to Qiu's empty seat. [[Qiu Jiongjiong|The director]], in modern attire, sits down and is served a bowl of Meng-po soup. == Cast == * Yi Sicheng as Qiu Fu, a renowned Sichuan opera actor of the New-New Theatre School ** Chen Haoyu as young Qiu Fu, a seven-year-old foundling who becomes an opera student * Guan Nan as Tong Huafeng, Qiu's wife * Qiu Zhimin as Pocky, a military commander, opera enthusiast, and the founder of the New-New Theatre School * Gu Tao as Crooky, a servant at the New-New Theatre School who eventually becomes an inn owner in the netherworld * Xue Xuchun as: ** Ah Hei, Qiu's son ** Chicken Foot,{{efn|The Chicken foot god ({{lang-zh|t=雞腳神|link=no}}) is a [[gnome]]-like creature in Sichuanese mythology.}} a cook at Pocky's inn In addition, Liu Boyu and Huang Lingchao appear as [[Ox-Head and Horse-Face]], the envoys of the netherworld,{{Cite web |url=https://videolibrarian.com/reviews/film/a-new-old-play/ |title=A New Old Play (Jiao Má Táng Huì) |date=7 March 2023 |website=Video Librarian |last=Fennessy |first=Kathy |access-date=23 March 2025}} while director [[Qiu Jiongjiong]] made a cameo appearance as himself.{{rp|294}} == Production == === Conception === {{quote box|quote="I began to piece together the story of an ordinary man, a man who embodied the spirit of a clown, living through the greatest upheavals of our times. There is nothing new under the sun, as we know. However, these characters are just like you and me, and we each in our own way will continue to repeat this same song of humanity."|source=—Qiu Jiongjiong, the director and writer, on the inspiration behind the screenplay for ''A New Old Play''|align=right|width=33%}} Qiu Fu, the grandfather of director [[Qiu Jiongjiong]], was a [[Sichuan opera]] actor who gained fame for playing [[Chou role|''chou'' roles]]{{efn|''Chou'' role ({{lang-zh|t=丑角|labels=no}}) is literally translated as "[[clown]] role" in English, although ''xiaochou'' (小丑), the Chinese term for clown, carries different connotations compared to ''chou'' role in Sichuan opera.}} in the 1930s and 1940s throughout [[Sichuan]]. He died in 1987 when Qiu Jiongjiong was ten years old.{{Cite book |last=Berry |first=Michael |date=13 July 2023 |title=畫外音：當代華語片影人對談錄 |trans-title=Voiceover: Conversations with Contemporary Chinese filmmakers |publisher=Showwe |isbn=9789864458189}}{{rp|293}} Growing up in [[Leshan]], Sichuan, Qiu Jiongjiong developed an interest in Sichuan opera influenced by his grandfather, which ultimately inspired him to pursue a career in filmmaking.{{Cite web |url=https://cinema-scope.com/cinema-scope-magazine/send-in-the-clowns-qiu-jiongjiong-on-a-new-old-play/ |title=Send in the Clowns: Qiu Jiongjiong on "A New Old Play" |date=15 September 2022 |website=[[Cinema Scope]] |last=Kraicer |first=Shelly |access-date=25 March 2025}} He also described having a "close" relationship with his grandfather, who served as a "crucial figure in [his] artistic inspirations" for his artworks and films. After making the documentary film ''{{ill|Mr. Zhang Believes|zh|癡 (2014年紀錄片)}}'' (2015), Qiu struggled with inspiration for several years despite still wanting to create films. In 2017, on the 30th anniversary of Qiu Fu's death, Qiu Jiongjiong's father began writing a [[biography]] to commemorate Qiu Fu and asked Qiu to illustrate for the book.{{Cite web |url=https://www.mirrormedia.mg/story/20220706insight009 |title=川劇世家出身戲班長大 他最討厭別人以這兩種眼光看待 |trans-title=Growing Up in a Sichuan Opera Family; He Dislikes Being Viewed in These Two Ways. |date=16 July 2022 |website=[[Mirror Media]] |author=項貽斐 |access-date=25 March 2025 |language=zh}} After creating illustrations for all 15 chapters in two months, Qiu felt a sense of "incompleteness" and wanted to approach the subject of his grandfather "through the medium of film", which inspired him to start writing the screenplay that would become ''A New Old Play''. It marks the second film produced by Qiu Jiongjiong featuring Qiu Fu, following the documentary short film ''Ode to Joy'' (2007), which depicted a stage performance in remembrance of the 20th anniversary of Qiu Fu's death and was cited by Qiu as a significant inspiration for ''A New Old Play''{{'s}} focus on the lives of ordinary people. === Pre-production === Qiu Jiongjiong began writing the screenplay in May 2017 and completed it in February 2018, taking about seven months to finish a script that exceeded 100,000 words.{{rp|293}} He based the story on his father's biography, along with some additional background research. It marks Qiu's seventh film and first [[Narrative film|fictional feature]].{{Cite web |url=https://funscreen.tfai.org.tw/article/37974 |title=【2022 北影】焦點影人邱炯炯：《姑奶奶》與邱炯炯的小丑精神 |trans-title=[2022 Taipei Film Festival] Filmmaker in Focus Qiu Jiongjiong: ''Madame'' and Qiu Jiongjiong's Clown Spirit. |date=4 July 2022 |website=[[Funscreen Weekly]] |last=Yip |first=Swani |access-date=25 March 2025 |language=zh}} Qiu described the story itself as "[[non-fictional]]", and he only aimed to create a sense of fiction through the film's aesthetics, drawing inspiration from both Chinese and Western stage plays.{{rp|289}} The screenplay emphasises Qiu Fu's status as a ''chou'', which Qiu Jiongjiong referred to as the "clown spirit", calling it the "core and quintessence of his cinematic grammar". He cited [[Federico Fellini]]'s works as an inspiration, highlighting how [[circus clown]]s served as [[viewpoint character]]s in his films.{{rp|288}} In Sichuan opera, ''chou'' roles (clowns) are usually not essential to the storyline but serve as the focal point, which Qiu referred to as the "author's perspective". In addition to Qiu Fu, Qiu Jiongjiong also created other clown-like characters, such as Crooky and Chicken Foot. These characters exist beyond the chronological timeline and the boundaries of the living and the dead in the plot, allowing them to serve as [[narrator]]s and [[Storytelling|storyteller]]s. He utilised these characters to interject the narrative to create a [[distancing effect]],{{Cite web |url=https://www.mirrormedia.mg/story/20220706insight010 |title=邱炯炯：四川人幽默無止境 「小丑精神」貫穿創作核心 |trans-title=Qiu Jiongjiong: Sichuanese Humor is Endless; the "Clown Spirit" is the Core of [His] Creations. |date=16 July 2022 |website=[[Mirror Media]] |author=項貽斐 |access-date=9 April 2025 |language=zh}} but rather than directly [[breaking the fourth wall]], Qiu aimed to re-examine the story naturally from the narrator and storyteller's perspectives. Qiu drew inspiration from his personal experiences and [[Sichuanese culture]] for the portrayal of clowns, noting that [[Sichuanese people]] are known for their optimism and [[Dark humor|dark sense of humour]] despite facing fate and suffering, qualities he found resonant with clowns' modest demeanor and playful exterior. Qiu also referenced the [[Great Chinese Famine]] in the film, a topic often omitted in other [[epic film]]s like ''[[Farewell My Concubine (film)|Farewell My Concubine]]'' and ''[[The Blue Kite]]'' (both 1993), explaining that he included it because he based the story primarily on his grandfather's biography and aimed to restore the original narrative. However, he noted that there are limited records about his grandfather's life during the [[Cultural Revolution]], and he had interviewed an elderly person knowledgeable about his grandfather's adoption of an infant girl for additional information. He concluded the screenplay with an [[Anticlimax (narrative)|anticlimax]] to reflect the daily lives of ordinary people, noting that while their stories may lack a [[Character arc|climactic arc]], they can still convey profound emotional depth.{{rp|296}} The project was showcased at the [[Golden Horse Film Festival and Awards|Golden Horse Project Promotion]] in November 2017, where it won the CNC Prize from the [[Centre national du cinéma et de l'image animée]].{{Cite web |url=https://star.ettoday.net/news/1058685 |title=馬來西亞電影2度抱走百萬首獎！金馬創投會議得獎出爐 |trans-title=A Malaysian Film Wins the Million-Dollar Grand Prize For The Second Time! Golden Horse Project Promotion Announces Winners. |date=23 November 2017 |website=[[ETtoday]] |author=洪文 |access-date=25 March 2025 |language=zh}} In May 2018, it received the Hubert Bals Fund at the [[International Film Festival Rotterdam]], under the [[working title]] ''The Neo-New Adventures'',{{Cite web |url=https://www.screendaily.com/news/rotterdams-hubert-bals-fund-announces-30th-anniversary-selection-expands-post-production-efforts/5129390.article |title=Rotterdam's Hubert Bals Fund announces 30th anniversary selection, expands post-production efforts |date=15 May 2018 |website=[[Screen Daily]] |last=Dalton |first=Ben |access-date=25 March 2025}}{{Cite web |url=https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/354483/ |title=IFFR announces Hubert Bals Fund 2018 spring selection |date=15 May 2018 |website=[[Cineuropa]] |access-date=25 March 2025}}{{efn|In an interview with ''[[Cinema Scope]]'', Qiu Jiongjiong referred to the working title as ''The Adventures of the New-New Theatre''.}} named after the opera troupe established at the film's opening. The first [[table-read]] took place in the same month, and the cast was given a year to prepare for their characters.{{Cite web |url=https://www.mirrormedia.mg/story/20220706insight008 |title=策展人變電影男主角 氣質對味、深入角色越演越自如 |trans-title=From Film Festival Curator to Film Protagonist; A Natural Fit, Deepening the Role with Each Performance. |date=16 July 2022 |website=[[Mirror Media]] |author=項貽斐 |access-date=25 March 2025 |language=zh}} Most of the actors and crew members are Qiu's family and friends, with many crew members also appeared in minor roles in the film. He cast them because he wanted to tell the story "locally", and described the shoot as a "party" among his closed ones. Yi Sicheng, a film festival curator who befriended Qiu at the YunFest Film Festival and made a brief appearance in ''Mr. Zhang Believes'', was invited by Qiu to star in the lead role. Qiu chose to avoid casting an actor of a similar age to the character Qiu Fu, as he felt the demeanor of actors around the same age as the character was unsuitable, and he was drawn to Yi's "old-timer" vibes, which he described as both "elegant and resilient". Guan Nan (who portrayed Tong Huafeng) and Xue Xuchan (who played dual roles as Hei and Chicken Foot) were also both film festival curators. Qiu chose Xue for the role of Chicken Foot due to his comedic awareness, and Xue received dialect coaching to prepare for his characters, as Hei speaks in [[Southwestern Mandarin]] while Chicken Foot uses the [[Leshan dialect]] with an [[Emeishan City|Emei]] accent. Qu Tao, an independent documentary filmmaker, was cast as the [[Aphasia|aphasic]] character Crooky, specifically designed by Qiu because he believed Qu would struggle to remember the character's lines. Qiu Zhimin and Chen Haoyu, who played Pocky and young Qiu Fu, are Qiu Jiongjiong's father and nephew, respectively. Despite initially hesitating to cast his father due to his age, Qiu Jiongjiong ultimately agreed when his father volunteered for the role, noting his similarities to Pocky.{{Cite web |url=https://theinitium.com/article/20230405-culture-film-interview-qiujiongjiong |title=導演/畫家邱炯炯專訪：我們的時代缺少解風情的眼光 |trans-title=Director/Visual artist Qiu Jiongjiong Exclusive Interview: Our Era Lacks a Perspective to Appreciate Romance. |date=4 April 2023 |website=[[Initium Media]] |author=張書瑋 |access-date=25 March 2025 |language=zh}} Qiu's cousin composed the film's score, drawing on elements from Sichuan opera, while his uncle served as the artistic advisor. Qiu Jiongjiong made a cameo appearance at the end of the film, citing his reasons as being both the author and part of the [[family history]] central to the story, as well as his desire to become part of the history of clowns as both a descendant and an enthusiast.{{rp|294}} All actors, except for the troupe teachers, were untrained, while the troupe roles were filled by professional Sichuan opera actors. === Production design === [[File:ANewOldPlayBoatScene.png|thumb|left|The film utilised visibly fake backdrops and set design, such as white fabrics to mimic turbulent waves during the disbandment scene of the New-New Theatre School, a style reminiscent of stage plays]] Set construction spanned about six months. The shoot took place entirely at a factory owned by a friend of Qiu's, with the production set constructed in a [[textile mill]] covering approximately 400 square meters (~4,306 square feet). A white shed was also built in the factory's parking lot, bringing the total size of the sets to about 1,000 square meters (~10,764 square feet). It was also the filming location for Qiu's previous film ''Mr. Zhang Believes'', for which he wrote the screenplay with that set in mind.{{rp|293}} He likened the production style to the works of [[Italo Calvino]], and explained that he chose a similar set design with ''Mr. Zhang Believes'' because he saw handcrafted production design as "an extension of creative invention", aiming to "refurbish through techniques" from early screen and stage plays. Qiu Jiongjiong (who was a trained visual artist) served as the art director and participated in creating the set props.{{Cite web |url=https://www.mirrormedia.mg/story/20220706insight006 |title=川劇名丑百年風情畫 《椒麻堂會》手工美學舉重若輕 |trans-title=A Century of Sichuan Opera's Famous Clowns; The Handcrafted Aesthetics of ''A New Old Play''. |date=12 July 2022 |website=[[Mirror Media]] |author=項貽斐 |access-date=25 March 2025 |language=zh}} The set was mainly decorated with hand-painted artwork, while all the props, walls, staircases, and backdrops were also hand-crafted. Most materials used for the set renovations were sourced directly from the surrounding factory, primarily utilising cloth, along with cardboard, wood, and cotton. Qiu emphasised that he chose to use "exaggerated" set and props to suit the film's tone of absurdity and [[black humour]].{{rp|289}} He also created and manipulated a "sense of alienation" through low-budget filmmaking, using visibly fake backgrounds and a theatrical style of production sets, influenced by [[Bertolt Brecht]]'s plays. For instance, a grey cloth was used to represent a river, while wind-blown plastic bags and shaking white fabrics were used to mimic the turbulent waves,{{Cite web |url=https://www.zaobao.com/entertainment/story20230312-1371693 |title=你说历史是一出戏 |trans-title=You Say History Is a Play. |date=12 March 2023 |website=[[Lianhe Zaobao]] |last=Wong |first=Lung Hsiang |access-date=6 April 2025 |language=zh}} with critics comparing the scantily decorated settings to [[Roy Andersson]]'s films. Lin Sheng-wei at ''[[United Daily News]]'' compared the "flimsy" and simplistic scenery to [[stage play]]s, calling it a "forced [[defamiliarization]]" that required the audience to "use their imagination in every scene", which encourages the audience to focus on the characters and immerse in their emotions to "make the absurd props come to life";{{Cite web |url=https://opinion.udn.com/opinion/story/10124/6520386 |title=中國藝術家邱炯炯的虛實技法：招引川劇魂魄入電影 |trans-title=Chinese Artist Qiu Jiongjiong's Techniques of Blending Reality and Illusion: Inviting the Soul of Sichuan Opera into Film. |date=8 August 2022 |website=[[United Daily News]] |last=Lin |first=Sheng-wei |access-date=16 March 2025 |language=zh}} while ''[[34th Street Magazine]]''{{`s}} Weike Li described the "obviously contrived sets" as "intentionally creating a sense of comical foreignness", presenting history in [[expressionism]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.34st.com/article/2023/02/chinese-a-new-old-play-clown-craftsmanship-mythology |title="A New Old Play": Clown Spirit and Handmade Craftsmanship |date=20 February 2023 |website=[[34th Street Magazine]] |last=Li |first=Weike |access-date=25 March 2025}} While designing the [[Youdu|netherworld]], Qiu cited [[Jacques Tati]]'s visual style as an inspiration, and made limited distinctions from the living world sets, primarily by dimming the [[Film lighting|lighting]] and using black-coloured props instead of white. === Filming === [[File:Leshan (16989556077).jpg|thumb|right|Filming took place at Qiu Jiongjiong's hometown [[Leshan]]]] [[Principal photography]] began in August 2019 in Leshan, Sichuan, China, the hometown of Qiu Jiongjiong. Filming lasted a total of 83 days over a three-month period.{{Cite web |url=https://www.dgeneratefilms.com/post/a-new-old-play-director-qiu-jiongjiong-interviewed-by-producer-ding-ningyuan |title=A NEW OLD PLAY: Director Qiu Jiongjiong Interviewed by Producer Ding Ningyuan |date=17 March 2022 |website=[[DGenerate Films]] |last=Wang |first=John Pao-chuan |access-date=25 March 2025}} Robbin Feng served as the cinematographer,{{Cite web |url=https://variety.com/2023/film/news/caa-china-genre-film-initiative-hong-kong-1235709109/ |title=CAA China Launches Genre Film Initiative in Hong Kong |date=31 August 2023 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |last=Frater |first=Patrick |access-date=5 April 2025}} using an [[Arri Alexa]] for the shoot, a camera model that Qiu described as "better than anything [he had] worked with before". In terms of cinematography, [[Tracking shot|horizontal shifts]] and [[Panning (camera)|lateral camera movements]] were primarily employed to present the composition as an "unveiling scroll of [[Chinese painting]]". The composition was mainly planimetric, with the camera positioned at a 90-degree angle to the actors and utilising perpendicular [[tracking shot]]s. Qiu aimed to convey a sense of [[Epic poetry|epic]] scale by emphasising the shallow depth of field in the set design, and compared the composition to the [[triptych]]s and [[frescoes]] of [[Giotto di Bondone]]. The production team planned the shooting schedule in advance, allowing set pieces to be disassembled and reassembled between scenes. The costumes used in the film were all from Qiu Jiongjiong's father's former opera troupe. The entire cast stayed in Leshan for a month after filming to record their dialogues, as no sounds were [[Sound recording and reproduction|recorded on location]] during filming.{{Cite web |url=https://p-articles.com/critics/3651.html |title=《椒麻堂會》：一場生死的流水席 |trans-title=''A New Old Play'': A Banquet of Life and Death |date=10 March 2023 |website=[[P-articles]] |author=朱嘉喬 |access-date=25 March 2025 |language=zh}} Qiu cited several reasons for this decision, including to avoid the high costs of on-site recording, the background noises at the factory, and the fact that most of the actors were non-locals who could not speak in standard Leshan dialects, therefore he decided to record dialogue after the filming wrapped. He also noted that it could enable the dialects to be delivered more precisely, allowing actors to adjust their emotions for a better performance, while [[crowd scene]]s and scenes without visible lip movements also permit changes to the dialogue. He chose to feature the film's dialogues in [[Sichuanese dialects|Sichuanese]], his native language, which he described as "vivid and humorous" and having a "strong nostalgia" stemming from the dialect's evolution over hundreds of years since [[Sichuanese people|the diaspora]] from other [[Provinces of China|provinces]] during the [[Ming Dynasty]]. This film is the second to be made primarily in Sichuanese since ''Conscription'' (1962). [[Dubbing]] was supervised by [[sound designer]] Wang Ran, who also created all the sound effects for the film. === Post-production === Post-production took place in France, with Qiu also serving as the editor.{{Cite web |url=https://www.screendaily.com/features/locarno-2021-line-up-guide-piazza-grande-and-international-competition-titles/5162237.article |title=Locarno 2021 line-up guide: Piazza Grande and International Competition titles |date=5 August 2021 |website=[[Screen Daily]] |last=Baughan |first=Nikki |access-date=15 April 2025}} French filmmaker {{ill|Marie-Pierre Duhamel-Muller|fr|Marie-Pierre Duhamel-Muller}}, who edited ''Mr. Zhang Believes'', was also involved in the editing through [[video conference]]s and provided advice on restructuring the narrative. The film features two parallel narratives, one set in the living world and the other in the netherworld, with both timelines unfolding [[Linear narrative|linearly]] and the living world timeline is interspersed into the netherworld timeline as [[Flashback (narrative)|flashbacks]].{{rp|293–294}} Producer Ding Ningyuan described the post-production process as "tense" due to budget constraints and the need to meet deadlines for film festivals. The film is co-produced by Hong Kong's Uluka Productions and France's Hippocampe Productions. Parallax, the rights division of Midnight Blur Films, managed its international sales.{{Cite web |url=https://variety.com/2021/film/news/parallax-midnight-blur-tokyo-1235104261/ |title=Chinese Distributor Parallax Picks Its Film Market Battles, Focuses on Tokyo |date=3 November 2021 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |last=Davis |first=Rebecca |access-date=27 March 2025}} The film was presented at the [[Entertainment Expo Hong Kong|Hong Kong-Asia Film Financing Forum]] in June 2020,{{Cite web |url=https://variety.com/2020/film/asia/haf-works-in-progress-online-film-project-market-1234645828/ |title=HAF Adds Works in Progress to Online Film Project Market |date=22 June 2020 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |last=Frater |first=Patrick |access-date=27 March 2025}} and at [[Marché du Film]] in July 2021, where it was retitled ''A New Old Play''.{{Cite web |url=https://www.screendaily.com/features/cannes-2021-hong-kong-and-china-hot-projects/5161218.article |title=Cannes 2021: Hong Kong and China hot projects |date=6 July 2021 |website=[[Screen Daily]] |last=Wong |first=Silva |access-date=27 March 2025 |archive-date=10 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250410162833/https://www.screendaily.com/features/cannes-2021-hong-kong-and-china-hot-projects/5161218.article |url-status=live }} Regarding the film titles, Qiu named the film ''Jiaoma tanghui'' ({{lang-zh|t=椒麻堂會}}) in Chinese.{{efn|''Jiaoma'' ({{lang-zh|t=椒麻|labels=no}}) refers to the spicy bite of [[Sichuan pepper]], a common flavor in [[Sichuan cuisine]], while ''tanghui'' ({{lang-zh|t=堂會|labels=no}}) refers to private banquets hosted by the wealthy, such as weddings or funerals, featuring entertainers.}} He literally translated the Chinese title to "The Gathering and Celebration of Peppery and Chili Flavors", which reflects the main character Qiu Fu's roots and occupation as a performer both before and after death and he felt it more accurately described the film. The English title, ''A New Old Play'', was suggested by the producer and the English subtitles translator, which Qiu found captured the film's themes of "history endlessly repeating itself" and evoking "a sense of [[déjà vu]]". In November 2021, the film was also showcased at TIFFCOM, [[Tokyo International Film Festival]]'s project market. == Themes == === Portrayal of history === ''A New Old Play'' chronicles a series of [[History of China#Modern China|Chinese historical events from the 1920s to the 1980s]], including the collapse of the [[Qing dynasty]], the [[Warlord Era]], [[World War II]] and the [[Nanjing Massacre|fall of Nanking]], the [[Chinese Civil War]], [[Mao Zedong]]'s [[Chinese Communist Party|Communist Party rule]], the [[Great Chinese Famine]], the [[Great Leap Forward]], and the [[Cultural Revolution]].{{Cite web |url=https://kdhx.org/articles/film-reviews/2704-%E2%80%98a-new-old-play%E2%80%99-provides-a-dense-chinese-political-and-cultural-history |title='A New Old Play' provides a dense Chinese political and cultural history |date=25 May 2022 |website=[[KDHX]] |last=Carson |first=Diane |access-date=16 March 2025}} Qiu Jiongjiong identified a theme of the film as the notion that history endlessly repeats itself. He summarised that the film's overall tone conveys the tragedy of destiny, aiming to create a contrast between the vividness of each individual and the cruelty of their irresistible fates.{{rp|292}} Qiu also explained that he found many historical narratives focus on context or abstract ideologies, but when the emphasis is placed on particular individuals, it becomes easier to "identify certain problems".{{Cite web |url=https://www.mirrormedia.mg/story/20220706insight007 |title=歷史悲劇輪迴上演 邱炯炯關照個體應對、產生自省 |trans-title=Historical Tragedies are Repeating; Qiu Jiongjiong Reflects on Individual Responses and Self-Examination. |date=16 July 2022 |website=[[Mirror Media]] |author=項貽斐 |access-date=10 April 2025}} Film scholar {{ill|Hao Jian|zh|郝建}} specifically commented on the film's approach to presenting [[historical memory]] through familial and personal experiences, which aligns with [[Michel Foucault]]'s discourse on popular memory and allows for a "faithful" portrayal of history, but from a new perspective that reinterprets and questions history—specifically, in the case of ''A New Old Play'', from the perspective of a clown and infused with a sense of comedy.{{Cite journal |last=Hao |first=Jian |date=2 May 2024 |title=紅色迴旋曲：1978年以來的中國電影與政治 |trans-title=Red Rhapsody: Chinese Cinema and Politics Since 1978 |journal=[[Sixiang]] |volume=50 |publisher=[[Linking Publishing]] |pages=103–150}}{{rp|145–146}} Qiu stated that he did not intend to recreate historical scenes but rather aimed to convey a general sense of the historical context of that time through metaphorical expressions, such as the film's simplistic and theatrical production style. Academic Isha Ting noted that the film's aesthetics resonate with Brecht's distancing effect, which encourages the audience to focus on social roots and structures while reflecting on what can be transformed. === Sichuanese culture === {{quote box|quote="In this film, the connection between those onstage and offstage, as well as inside and outside the Sichuan opera being put together in the story, is blurred. What happens onstage is integrated into the narrative, and the expressions onstage are blended into the characters' everyday lives. This is because Sichuan opera took root in my body and soul through the mundanity of everyday life. Just like when generations of Sichuan opera goers, who spent much of their time in the theater weeping, sighing, falling asleep, etc., their lives are in a way inter-textualized with the performance on stage, creating an adventitious symmetry of life itself; were they just watching a performance, or are they themselves a part of, or even integrated into the performance?"|source=—Qiu Jiongjiong on incorporating the characteristics of Sichuan opera into the narrative|align=right|width=33%}} Qiu described his motive for creating ''A New Old Play'' as a desire to craft a "Sichuan-flavored saga", incorporating local elements without reducing them to conceptualised spectacles or [[stereotype]]s. Notable elements added to the film include [[Sichuanese people]], [[Sichuan opera]], and [[Sichuanese dialects]], all heavily influenced by the culture surrounding him during his upbringing.{{Cite web |url=http://epaper.ynet.com/html/2023-01/13/content_411069.htm?div=0 |title=《椒麻堂会》：椒麻味儿的"寻梦环游记" |trans-title=''A New Old Play'': A Spicy-falvored ''Coco''. |date=13 January 2023 |website=[[Beijing Youth Daily]] |access-date=16 March 2025 |language=zh}} Regarding Sichuan opera, Qiu sought to transform the traditional operatic language into a more accessible form of expression that could effectively communicate while retaining its flavor and melodies, sharing similarities with the works of [[Geoffrey Chaucer]], [[François Rabelais]], and [[Giovanni Boccaccio]]. Despite featuring exaggerated theatrical staging in its production design, film scholar {{ill|Michael Berry (scholar)|lt=Michael Berry|zh|白睿文}} observed that these production values closely parallel Sichuan opera, which enhance the authenticity and emotional depth of the performances while maintaining the overall tone of [[Realism (arts)|realism]].{{rp|292}} Qiu identified the characteristics of Sichuan opera as "mundanity of everyday life" filled with expressions of deep and personal humanity, and he integrated these characteristics into the story, blending the ordinary with the daily lives of the characters. He compared the viewing experience to that of opera-goers [[Intertextuality|inter-textualizing]] with the stage performances, creating a symmetry with their own lives and immersing themselves in the performance. Scholar {{ill|Wong Nim-yan|zh|黃念欣}} also recognised this perspective, noting that there are limited Sichuan opera scenes in the film, but the cinematography, production design, and dialogues strongly resemble it, and compared its central thought to traditional Sichuan opera pieces like ''Inn of Successive Promotion'' ({{lang-zh|t=連升店|labels=no}}) and ''Writing Essays'' ({{lang-zh|t=做文章|labels=no}}), suggesting that the film itself can be viewed as a form of Sichuan opera.{{Cite web |url=https://news.mingpao.com/pns/%E4%BD%9C%E5%AE%B6%E5%B0%88%E6%AC%84/article/20230328/s00018/1679937927887/%E4%B8%96%E7%B4%80-%E5%A4%95%E6%8B%BE%E6%9C%9D%E8%8A%B1-%E5%9B%9B%E5%B7%9D%E5%A5%BD%E6%88%B2 |title=世紀．夕拾朝花：四川好戲 |trans-title=Century．Morning Flowers Collected at Dusk: The Good Play of Szechwan. |date=28 March 2023 |website=[[Ming Pao]] |last=Wong |first=Nim-yan |access-date=6 April 2025 |language=zh}} The film also explores [[thanatology]], which Qiu describes as stemming from the Sichuanese people's understanding of life and death.{{rp|294}} A significant part of the film is set in the [[underworld]], using a secular perspective to speculate about the [[afterlife]].{{rp|294}} He found that the Sichuanese people hold an optimistic view of death, citing traditional ''Ba Ba banquets'' ({{lang-zh|t=壩壩宴|labels=no}}), family banquets held for both weddings and funerals, as an example and describing them as a reflection of the Sichuanese perspective on death as "a harmony between sorrow and joy". He composed the story in which the protagonist reflects on his life and anticipates his post-death journey, aligning it with Sichuanese views on death and describing the film as "a flowing banquet of life and death".{{rp|294}} == Distribution == === Release === ''A New Old Play'' had its world premiere in competition for the [[Golden Leopard]] at the [[74th Locarno Film Festival]] on 13 August 2021.{{Cite web |url=https://www.locarnofestival.ch/LFF/program/archive/film/Jiao-ma-tang-hui?fid=1217378&eid=74 |title=Jiao ma tang hui |date=1 July 2021 |website=[[Locarno Film Festival]] |access-date=18 March 2025 |archive-date=28 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028205209/https://www.locarnofestival.ch/LFF/program/archive/film/Jiao-ma-tang-hui?fid=1217378&eid=74 |url-status=dead }} It was subsequently screened in the A Window on Asian Cinema section at the [[26th Busan International Film Festival]],{{Cite web |url=https://www.tatlerasia.com/lifestyle/entertainment/busan-international-film-festival-2021-full-list-program-list |title=Busan International Film Festival 2021: Full Movie Lineup |date=16 September 2021 |website=[[Tatler Asia]] |last=Soriano |first=Jianne |access-date=18 March 2025}} in competition for the Golden Apricot at the [[Yerevan International Film Festival|18th Yerevan International Film Festival]], for the Montgolfière d'Or at the [[Three Continents Festival|47th Three Continents Festival]], and for the [[Silver Screen Award]] at the [[32nd Singapore International Film Festival]].
